title: One Obstruction, Three Faces — Merle Lean stack, with Lean 4 formalisations of Halbeisen–Hungerbühler 1997, Lagarias 1990, Steiner 1978, Seifert 1988 and Brox 2000
description:
Lean 4 verification stack of Eric Merle (the “kernel key”) for the joint note One obstruction, three faces with Benjamin Macindoe, together with Lean 4 formalisations of four classical papers: L. Halbeisen and N. Hungerbühler, “Optimal bounds for the length of rational Collatz cycles”, Acta Arithmetica 78 (1997), 227–239, J. C. Lagarias, “The set of rational cycles for the 3x+1 problem”, Acta Arithmetica 56 (1990), 33–53, B. G. Seifert, “On the arithmetic of cycles for the Collatz–Hasse (‘Syracuse’) conjectures”, Discrete Mathematics 68 (1988), 293–298, and T. Brox, “Collatz cycles with few descents”, Acta Arithmetica 92 (2000), 181–188; and of a classical theorem, R. P. Steiner, “A theorem on the Syracuse problem”, Congressus Numerantium 20 (1978), 553–559, reconstructed from published accounts, proved under a named hypothesis in steiner1978/ and without it in logs23/; and, in sdw2005/, Lean proofs of upper bounds for the number of odd terms of a cycle with at most 82 or 91 local minima, in the way of J. Simons and B. de Weger, “Theoretical and computational bounds for m-cycles of the 3n+1-problem”, Acta Arithmetica 117 (2005), 51–70, weaker than their final bounds, without G. Rhin's lower bound.

hh1997/ (Lean 4.34.0, Mathlib v4.34.0): every result that the paper proves is kernel-checked (71 proved statements, 70 up to release v1.6, each frozen before its proof was written), with no sorry in the proofs, no native_decide, and only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Remark 1 for l > 10³ (the bound 1/2), for which the paper gives no proof, was stated and not proved up to release v1.6; it is proved since 2026-11-07 against its statement frozen on 2026-10-19. K. Knight's preprint (HAL hal-04261183v1, 2023) states, without proof and only for l = ⌈n log₂ 3⌉, the constants 1/2 and 1/6; here 1/6 is proved for every l ≥ 2 and 1/2 only for l > 10³ (with ≤; Knight's inequalities are strict). Remark 2 and two figures the paper quotes from other authors are not formalised. The formalisation proves nothing new about Collatz cycles. See hh1997/README.md, which also lists the points found in the paper.

lagarias1990/ (Lean 4.34.0, Mathlib v4.34.0): 60 frozen statements, all proved (61 theorems, since Corollary 2.1a is proved twice), each statement written before its proof (git records this order for the last six), with no sorry in the proofs, no native_decide, and only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Theorem 3.1 with the printed constant and Theorem 3.2 are proved under named hypotheses (the prime number theorem; the bound (3.3), a consequence of the Baker–Fel’dman bound), which are hypotheses of the theorems, not axioms; Theorem 3.1 is also proved without any hypothesis, with the constant 6/5 instead of 5/4. Out of scope: Theorems 3.3 and 4.3, the bounds (4.12)–(4.14), Remarks (2)–(4) of p. 52 with (4.19), and the flat segment of Fig. 4.1. The minimality of the 48 unchanged rows of Table 3.1 is checked numerically, not in Lean. For the results in scope, where we found a slip in a printed statement or proof, the repaired version is proved; the slips found are listed next to what is printed in lagarias1990/README.md, and the list is not exhaustive. The formalisation proves nothing new about Collatz cycles.

steiner1978/ (Lean 4.34.0, Mathlib v4.34.0): the statements and the proof were written without the original paper; they are reconstructed from R. Steiner, Fibonacci Quarterly 19 (1981), 285–288, J. C. Lagarias’s annotated bibliography of the 3x+1 problem (entries 48, 158, 159) and J. Simons and B. de Weger, Acta Arithmetica 117 (2005), read in their version 1.44 (2010), §1.4 and Lemma 12. After release v1.2, on 2026-10-21, the paper was read in a scanned copy and compared with the statements: nothing in the Lean files changes (steiner1978/README.md, section Comparison with the original). Release v1.2 said that the original paper could not be accessed, and the frozen header of steiner1978/Steiner/Steiner_Enonces.lean (line 10, unchanged in this release) says that it was not available to us; these claims are withdrawn (steiner1978/README.md, Related work). 12 frozen statements, all proved, each statement written before its proof, with no sorry in the proofs, no native_decide, and only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Steiner’s theorem (the only circuit on the positive integers that is a cycle of the 3x+1 map is {1, 2}) is proved under a named hypothesis, the case u₀ = 0 of G. Rhin’s inequality (7) (Progress in Mathematics 71, 1987), called H_Rhin in the Lean files, which is a hypothesis of the theorems, not an axiom. Without any hypothesis it is proved, in steiner1978/, for at most 20000 odd terms, by a finite check certified by the kernel; this is far weaker than the published bounds that rest on computer verifications of the conjecture. It is proved without this hypothesis in logs23/ (below). The formalisation proves nothing new about Collatz cycles.

logs23/ (Lean 4.34.0, Mathlib v4.34.0; new in v1.4): Steiner’s theorem without the hypothesis H_Rhin. The proofs of steiner1978/ use H_Rhin only to bound the number k of odd terms, and what they need is much weaker: 1/(2^k − 1) ≤ |(k + l) log 2 − k log 3| for every k > 20000 and every l ≥ 0, which logs23/ proves. For k below 6.34·10^100 this follows from two consecutive convergents of log₂ 3, with enclosures of log 2 and log(3/2) computed by the kernel; for k ≥ 2^334, from an explicit, deliberately crude lower bound exp(−10^12 ν^5) ≤ |b₁ log 2 − b₂ log 3| for every natural b₁ and every natural b₂ ≥ 2^334, ν = ⌊log₂ b₂⌋ + 1, proved, after division by the gcd of b₁ and b₂ (small reduced denominators are handled by the convergents), with an interpolation determinant in the spirit of M. Laurent (Acta Arithmetica 66, 1994) and a positivity argument (Cauchy–Binet, Descartes’ rule of signs) in place of a zero lemma. Hence the statements steiner, steiner_int, steiner_cycle, steiner_cycle_int and tstar_circuit of steiner1978/ hold without their premise; in particular, with no hypothesis, the only circuit on the positive integers that is a cycle of the 3x+1 map is {1, 2}. 14 frozen statements, all proved, each statement written before its proof, with no sorry in the proofs, no native_decide, and only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Not proved: H_Rhin itself (Rhin’s paper is not formalised); the sixth statement of steiner1978/ with the premise H_Rhin, rhin_k_le, is not restated without it. The bound is far weaker than the published explicit bounds (Laurent 1994; M. Laurent, M. Mignotte and Y. Nesterenko 1995; N. Gouillon 2006). No novelty is claimed: replacing the zero lemma by positivity may well be known. The formalisation proves nothing new about Collatz cycles.

seifert1988/ (Lean 4.34.0, Mathlib v4.34.0; new in v1.6): 33 frozen statements, committed before their proofs, all proved, with no hypothesis, no sorry in the proofs, no native_decide, and only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The statements were compared on 2026-11-07 with the page images of the publisher’s PDF. With Definition 1.1 of the paper, the printed numerator (e) is that of the vector read backwards: it gives 7 and 13801 where the paper’s examples give 5 and 2363. Theorems 1 and 2 are proved along the paper’s lines once (e) and the exponent of Theorem 2 are read accordingly. As printed, Theorem 1(b) and Theorem 2 (read with the numerator of (1.3), since the display of Theorem 2 has a misprint) fail for ε = −1; for ε = +1 they are neither proved nor refuted. Corollary 1 fails only for the cycle (5 7) of f₋₁; this exact form is proved with a lower bound for |2^l − 3^r|, checked by the kernel for r ≤ 20000 and derived for larger r from the bound lam_lower of logs23/. The conclusion of Corollary 2 is the classical solution of 2^l − 3^r = ±1 (Levi ben Gerson) and is proved without its hypothesis. The slips found are listed in seifert1988/README.md and may well be known. The formalisation proves nothing new about Collatz cycles.

brox2000/ (Lean 4.34.0, Mathlib v4.34.0; new in v1.9): Lemma 2.2, Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 of Brox's paper, for all cycles of the map T(x) = x/2 (x even), (3x+1)/2 (x odd) on the integers, with Γ the set of odd elements of a cycle and δ(Γ) the number of its descending elements (x with 4 | 3x+1): the period of a cycle other than {0} is at most 2|Γ|, and for each n only finitely many cycles have |Γ| ≤ n (Lemma 2.2); only finitely many cycles have δ(Γ) < 2 log |Γ| (Theorem 1.1); for each ν, only finitely many cycles have δ(Γ) ≤ ν (Corollary 1.2). Theorem 1.1 is also proved in the explicit form δ(Γ) < 2 log |Γ| ⇒ |Γ| < 2^1500. This explicit form is not claimed as new: Brox's argument is effective (it uses a Baker–Fel’dman constant that is effectively computable; the paper gives no number), and our number comes from the crude lower bound of logs23/. The proof differs from Brox's at its core: on the positive integers it uses the chain of local minima and the lemmas of sdw2005/ with the lower bound of logs23/; on the negative integers, x ↦ −x turns the cycles of T into those of y/2 (y even), (3y−1)/2 (y odd), for which that chain and those lemmas are written again. 10 frozen statements (5 for the cycles on the positive integers, then 5 for all cycles), all proved, no hypothesis, no sorry, no native_decide, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The 5 statements for all cycles were written before their proofs and never changed, but committed after the proofs had been drafted (see brox2000/README.md). Brox's Remark 4.1 (3x + d) is not formalised. The formalisation proves nothing new about Collatz cycles and excludes no cycle.

The rest of the repository is the Merle side of the joint note; the status of each of its entries is the claims ledger of the shared repository macindoe/one-obstruction-three-faces, not this archive. Its six ledger Lean files (OneObstruction/) were first checked on Lean 4.27.0 and re-checked on Lean 4.34.0 (recheck-v4.34/RECHECK.md); recheck-v4.34/Labo/ holds lab modules offered for information (Lean 4.34.0; one sorry, the marker of the open target T★). Nothing in this repository excludes a Collatz cycle beyond the published bounds (Bařina's verification to 2^71; Hercher 2023, in the proof of which P. Norfleet reports an error, not checked here: see sdw2005/README.md).

v1.5 (documentation only): adds the file LICENSE, the official legal code of CC BY 4.0 (releases v1.0 to v1.4 contain no LICENSE file; their license is the one stated in their README and Zenodo record), a CITATION.cff file, a section of the root README on re-checking the formalisations of classical papers from a fresh clone, and dated notes in the READMEs. No Lean file, check script or recorded axiom report changes.

v1.6: adds seifert1988/. Outside it, no Lean file, check script or recorded axiom report changes. Documentation: the root README (the new folder, the DOI of v1.5, a dated note on the credit given to Seifert 1988 for ledger entry L-A1, re-checking), CITATION.cff and this record; and, from a documentation commit of 2026-11-06 made after v1.5, hh1997/README.md (a shasum line in the check commands), recheck-v4.34/LABO.md (how to print the axioms of the lab files) and the root README (cd after git clone; the re-checking section also covers recheck-v4.34/).

v1.7: proves remark1_large in hh1997/ (Remark 1 of Halbeisen–Hungerbühler, the bound 1/2 for l > 10³), against its statement frozen on 2026-10-19: new files hh1997/Labo/HH1997c_Demi_Preuves.lean and hh1997/Labo/HH1997c_Demi_Axiomes.lean, and the axiom log hh1997/axioms/HH1997c_Demi_Axiomes.txt; hh1997/check.sh now compiles 35 files instead of 33 and reads 85 axiom reports instead of 78; hh1997/SHA256SUMS is updated; the module doc comment of hh1997/Labo/HH1997c_Axiomes.lean gets a dated note (its axiom report is unchanged). No statement, no other Lean file and no other recorded axiom report changes. The constant 1/2 for l > 10³ is Halbeisen–Hungerbühler's; K. Knight's preprint (HAL hal-04261183v1, 2023) states, without proof and only for l = ⌈n log₂ 3⌉, the constants 1/6 and 1/2, and is now credited; its published version was not read. hh1997/ was re-checked from a fresh clone of commit 31e63a4 (exit 0, 85 axiom reports identical to the recorded ones). Documentation: hh1997/README.md, the root README (the DOI of v1.6, the re-check from a fresh clone), CITATION.cff (the DOI of v1.6) and this record.

v1.8: adds sdw2005/. Without G. Rhin's lower bound for |x log 2 + y log 3| and without a lower bound X0 for the elements of a cycle, it proves, with the lower bounds of logs23/ and by the method of the a priori bound of J. Simons and B. de Weger (version 1.44 of their paper read), upper bounds of its own for the number K of odd terms of a cycle of the map C(n) = n/2 (n even), (3n+1)/2 (n odd) on the positive integers with at most m local minima: K < 4·10^18 for m ≤ 82 and K < 2·10^21 for m ≤ 91. As bounds for all m ≤ 82 (resp. m ≤ 91), they are below the value at m = 82 (resp. m = 91) of the initial bound K1(m) of their Lemma 14, which uses Rhin's lower bound (by our computation from its equation; K1(m) grows with m and is smaller for small m), and above the final bounds of their Theorem 3(d). 9 frozen statements (committed before their proofs, with no proof file), all proved, no hypothesis, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. This is not new mathematics; it excludes no cycle and does not give a proof of C. Hercher's theorem (no nontrivial m-cycle with m ≤ 91; arXiv:2201.00406) without Rhin's lower bound; moreover, P. Norfleet's repository PhilNorfleet/Hercher2023_lean (SUMMARY.md, read on 2026-11-07) reports an error near the end of the proof of Theorem 21 of Hercher's paper (arXiv v3), which his proof for m ≤ 91 uses (not checked here; see sdw2005/README.md). sdw2005/ was re-run from a fresh GitHub clone of commit e2fdb2e (2026-11-07), with Lean 4.34.0 already installed and Mathlib's download cache already filled: exit 0, 8 minutes including lake exe cache get and the runs of steiner1978/check.sh and logs23/check.sh that sdw2005/check.sh starts, 9 axiom reports, sdw2005/axioms/Sdw2005_Axiomes.txt identical byte for byte to the log of the run. Outside sdw2005/, no Lean file, check script or recorded axiom report changes. Documentation: a dated credit note in logs23/README.md and the root README (the core of the method of logs23/, G. Pólya's count of real zeros used as the zero estimate of an interpolation determinant, is in M. Waldschmidt, Diophantine Approximation on Linear Algebraic Groups, Springer, 2000, §2.2–2.3); version 2 of the errata note (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24043129) cited in hh1997/README.md and lagarias1990/README.md; dated notes on the targets of ccchallenge records 15 and 16 in lagarias1990/README.md and steiner1978/README.md; the root README (the new folder, the DOI of v1.7, re-checking, a dated note on Hercher 2023), CITATION.cff (the DOI of v1.7) and this record.

v1.9: adds brox2000/ (above); and, in sdw2005/, the files Sdw2005/Pont_Enonces.lean (4 frozen statements, committed alone before their proofs) and Sdw2005/Pont.lean, which restate the bounds of v1.8 for the number of distinct odd values of a cycle, the count used by some other formalisations: pont_image and pont_image_91 for any period (with a hypothesis on the number of local-minimum terms), and pont_minimal and pont_minimal_91 over the minimal period (with a hypothesis on the number of distinct local-minimum values); sdw2005/check.sh now compiles 9 files instead of 7 and reads 13 axiom reports instead of 9, and sdw2005/Sdw2005/Axiomes.lean, sdw2005/SHA256SUMS and sdw2005/axioms/Sdw2005_Axiomes.txt are updated (the 9 earlier axiom reports are unchanged). brox2000/ was re-run from a fresh GitHub clone of commit 9077bda (2026-11-08), with Lean 4.34.0 already installed and Mathlib's download cache already filled: exit 0, 30 minutes including the clone, lake exe cache get and the runs of steiner1978/check.sh, logs23/check.sh and sdw2005/check.sh that brox2000/check.sh starts, 12 + 15 + 13 + 10 axiom reports (steiner1978/, logs23/, sdw2005/, brox2000/), sdw2005/axioms/Sdw2005_Axiomes.txt and brox2000/axioms/Brox2000_Axiomes.txt identical byte for byte to the axiom lines of the logs of the run. Outside sdw2005/ and brox2000/, no Lean file, check script or recorded axiom report changes. Documentation: sdw2005/README.md (status, the re-run of v1.9), brox2000/README.md, the root README (the new folder, the DOI of v1.8, re-checking), CITATION.cff (Brox 2000 in its title and message, the DOI of v1.8) and this record.

Source repository (with the git history cited in the READMEs): https://github.com/ericmerle3789/one-obstruction-three-faces-lean. Website: https://collatz-lab.org. License: CC BY 4.0.
